name: United States
key_conventions: Commonly called a 'resume', not a 'CV' (in the US, 'CV' is typically reserved for academic or research contexts)
Usually kept to 1 page, or up to 2 pages for more senior candidates
Typically no photo, date of birth, or marital status included
Often includes a brief summary or objective statement near the top
regulatory_considerations: US equal employment law discourages employers from requesting information like age, marital status, or a photo, so this is commonly left off resumes
Work authorization status is usually addressed separately during the application process, not necessarily stated on the resume itself
source_note: General conventions only, based on common US recruitment practice — individual employers and sectors vary, and the job description or application instructions should always take priority.
